learning_outcomes.text: Applies the principles of machine and mechanism theory.

Knows how to use simulation programs for the kinematics and dynamics of mechanisms, and understands the results obtained. Applies dynamic equilibrium in the study of a single-degree-of-freedom system. Understands and applies the reduction of dynamic parameters in single-degree-of-freedom systems. Correctly calculates the intrinsic parameters of a gear wheel. Designs cam mechanisms using computer programs.

syllabus_topics: Kinematics of rigid bodies I: Velocity analysis applied to machines and planar mechanisms of 1 GdL (Degrees of Freedom). 2.1. Graphical method. 2.2. Loop method. 2.3. Relative velocities method. 2.4. Numerical methods

Kinematics of rigid bodies II: Acceleration analysis applied to machines and planar mechanisms of 1 GdL (Degrees of Freedom). 2.1. Graphical method. 2.2. Loop method. 2.3. Relative velocities method. 2.4. Numerical methods.
Dynamics of rigid bodies I: Dynamic analysis of machines and planar mechanisms of 1 GdL (Degrees of Freedom). 3.1. D'Alembert's dynamic equilibrium method. 3.2. Principle of virtual powers.

Dynamics of rigid bodies II: Dynamic resolution of machines and planar mechanisms of 1 GdL (Degrees of Freedom). 4.1. Direct and inverse scalar resolution of machines and mechanisms. 4.2. Direct and inverse vectorial resolution of machines and mechanisms.
Design of cams, friction wheels, and gears. 5.1. Classification and dynamic analysis of cams and followers. 5.2. Friction wheels. 5.3. Kinematic and dynamic analysis of gears. 5.4. Gear trains.
Simple machines, belts, chains, and cables. 6.1. Kinematic and dynamic analysis of belt and pulley transmission. 6.2. Cables. 6.3. Sprocket and chain transmission.
teaching_methods: Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom

assessment_methods.method: Delivery exercises to be solved in pairs during the 2 hours of problem class
Written test of theoretical concepts and exercises (first test)
Written test of theoretical concepts and exercises (second test)

assessment_rules: For the first call, the average of the two development test scores must be 4.0 or higher to be averaged with other continuous assessment grades. Additionally, the minimum score for the second development test must be 4.0 or higher to be averaged. For the second call, the exam accounts for 80% of the grade, added to the 20% from delivery problems, provided the final exam score is 4.0 or higher. Fraudulent use of AI in evaluative tests is prohibited and leads to a failing grade for that activity, potentially resulting in disciplinary action.
